central_question: Can research-behavior specialization substantially improve the research competence of an approximately 8B open-weight language model?
scope: The primary comparison is an untouched Qwen3-8B-Base checkpoint versus a research-behavior SFT/QLoRA adapter on an unseen, source-grouped benchmark.

research_questions.question: Does research-behavior fine-tuning improve performance over the untouched base model on unseen research tasks?
Can a specialized approximately 8B model compete with a larger untuned general model on research-specific tasks?
How much training data is required before meaningful improvements appear?
Which task families provide the greatest benefit?
Does specialization increase citation and evidence discipline?
Does specialization improve recognition of insufficient evidence?
Does specialization damage useful general capabilities such as instruction following, basic reasoning, summarization, and technical explanation?

hypotheses.statement: The tuned 8B model will have higher macro-averaged structured validity and research-action accuracy than the untouched base on the frozen research benchmark.
The tuned model will improve citation precision/recall and lower unsupported-claim rate relative to the untouched base.
The tuned model will improve insufficient-evidence recognition on cases where the supplied sources do not establish the requested conclusion.
Evidence attribution, source selection, and methodology-critique families will show larger gains than generic planning families.
Specialization may regress at least one non-target capability unless the training mixture or a general-capability control is sufficient; this is a directional risk hypothesis, not an expected result.

analysis_plan.uncertainty: paired bootstrap confidence intervals over per-example metric differences where sample size and metric semantics support it
analysis_plan.multiple_comparisons: report task-family estimates descriptively and avoid treating every subgroup as an independent confirmatory test
analysis_plan.invalidity_rule: A run with malformed targets, non-finite loss, benchmark contamination, or an artifact hash mismatch is invalidated and not pooled with valid runs.

outcome_policy: No conclusion is recorded in this preregistration-style file. Results and deviations belong in immutable experiment manifests and the chronological research ledger.
